rationale: I picked the calls that can block the hot path for an unbounded time: every blocking syscall (sleeps, socket I/O, accept/connect, waitpid, file I/O) and every lock acquire that can wait (mutex, rwlock, spin, sem_wait). I also picked the indirect calls whose names show they lead to hidden locks or syscalls. I left out trylock because it never blocks, heap allocations because they are a lower-severity jitter cost, and the generic virtual and clean_fp indirect calls because they are most likely cheap or harmless callbacks.
